originalAction.text: Melphalan is a nitrogen-mustard alkylating drug. The cited label relates its cytotoxicity to interstrand DNA crosslinks, probably formed through binding at guanine, and states that it is active against both resting and rapidly dividing tumor cells. This molecular action is distinct from the anatomical route used to deliver the medicine. In the HEPZATO system, melphalan is administered through the hepatic artery using a specialized delivery and filtration procedure; that route does not establish benefit for every tumor involving the liver. The label states that its exposure-response relationship is not fully characterized and separately warns about myelosuppression despite regional delivery. The mechanism therefore supplies a rationale for cytotoxic activity, while response, survival and harms must be evaluated in the actual disease, product and treatment setting. Findings from liver-directed treatment cannot automatically be assigned to an oral or systemic melphalan regimen.

questions.title: Does regional delivery change the molecular mechanism?
questions.text: The label describes the same melphalan alkylating action, while the liver-directed system changes the delivery context. Its exposure-response relationship is not fully characterized, and regional delivery does not eliminate the reported risk of myelosuppression.
